title: Module 10 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

o: Means of two or more groups
items.why: It generalizes the independent t test to any number of groups.

items.q: Why not run several t tests instead of one ANOVA for three groups?
o: Each extra test raises the overall Type I error rate
items.why: With three tests at .05 the chance of at least one false alarm is about 14 percent, not 5.

o: Variance between groups divided by variance within groups
Variance within divided by variance between
The mean difference divided by SD
SS total divided by SS between
items.why: F = MS between divided by MS within. Under the null it is near 1.

o: Random variability among participants in the same condition
items.why: Within-group variability is error. It is the same whether or not the treatment works.

o: Differences among group means, plus error
items.why: If the null is true, between-group variance estimates the same error as within-group variance, so F is near 1.

items.why: It is SS between divided by SS total, an effect size for ANOVA.

o: At least one group mean differs from another, but not which
items.why: Follow-up post hoc tests identify the specific differences.

items.q: A post hoc test such as Tukey HSD
o: Compares pairs of means while controlling the overall Type I error
Is run only when F is not significant
items.why: Post hoc tests are used after a significant F and keep the familywise error rate in check.
